knowledge:
- key_parameters: files=Character vector of paths to LCMS/GCMS raw data files (e.g., NetCDF, mzXML) ;; mzbin=Bin size in m/z units used for combining mass spectra (e.g., 0.25) ;; SNR.Th=Signal-to-noise ratio threshold for mass peak detection ;; linear=Logical indicating whether to use linear interpolation when combining spectra ;; scales=Wavelet scales used for continuous wavelet transform (CWT) peak detection in the m/z domain ;; RTscales=Wavelet scales used for CWT peak detection in the retention time domain ;; RTSNR.Th=Signal-to-noise ratio threshold for chromatographic peak detection
- alternatives: xcms=cosmiq uses the xcms object structure and relies on xcms for retention time alignment (retcor) and peak table generation (peakTable). cosmiq is preferred over standard xcms peak detection when combining spectra across runs is desired to improve the detection of low-abundance peaks.
- when_to_use: Use this package when preprocessing high-resolution LCMS/GCMS data (e.g., from TOF or Q-TOF instruments) in metabolomics or lipidomics studies where alignment and detection of low-intensity features across multiple samples are critical.
- pitfalls: High-resolution LCMS datasets can be extremely large (e.g., 500MB per file), which may cause memory and performance issues. For testing or package builds, it is recommended to process a reduced m/z range. When running the step-by-step workflow, a dummy peak matrix must be manually created and assigned to the xcmsSet object before running xcms::retcor.

workflows.name: cosmiq_wrapper
workflows.intent: Preprocess LCMS/GCMS raw data files in a single step using the cosmiq wrapper function.
input: my.input.files (character vector of paths to raw LCMS/GCMS files, such as CDF or mzXML)
workflows.stages: 1. Identify input file paths ;; 2. Run the cosmiq wrapper function to combine spectra, detect peaks, correct retention times, and quantify features ;; 3. Visualize the resulting m/z versus RT map and inspect peak data.
workflows.code:
library(cosmiq)
cdfpath <- file.path(find.package("faahKO"), "cdf")

my.input.files <- dir(c(paste(cdfpath, "WT", sep='/'), 
	paste(cdfpath, "KO", sep='/')), full.names=TRUE)

# run cosmiq wrapper function
#
x <- cosmiq(files=my.input.files, mzbin=0.25, SNR.Th=0, linear=TRUE)
# 

# graph result
image(t(x$eicmatrix), main='mz versus RT map')
head(x$xs@peaks)

workflows.name: cosmiq_step_by_step
workflows.intent: Manually preprocess LCMS/GCMS data step-by-step to combine spectra, detect masses, align retention times, and quantify features.
input: my.input.files (character vector of paths to raw LCMS/GCMS files, such as CDF or mzXML)
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize xcmsSet object and define phenotype data ;; 2. Combine mass spectra across all scans and runs using combine_spectra ;; 3. Detect relevant mass peaks on the master spectrum using peakdetection ;; 4. Perform retention time alignment using xcms::retcor after creating a dummy peak matrix ;; 5. Generate the extracted ion chromatogram (EIC) matrix using eicmatrix ;; 6. Detect chromatographic peaks in the retention time domain using retention_time ;; 7. Quantify features and create the final data matrix using create_datamatrix ;; 8. Extract the final peak table using xcms::peakTable.
workflows.code:
library(cosmiq)
cdfpath <- file.path(find.package("faahKO"), "cdf")
my.input.files <- dir(c(paste(cdfpath, "WT", sep='/'), 
	paste(cdfpath, "KO", sep='/')), full.names=TRUE)

#
# create xcmsSet object
# todo
xs <- new("xcmsSet")
xs@filepaths <- my.input.files

class <- as.data.frame(c(rep("KO",6),rep("WT", 6)))
rownames(class) <- basename(my.input.files)
xs@phenoData <- class

x <- combine_spectra(xs=xs, mzbin=0.25, 
	linear=TRUE, continuum=FALSE)

plot(x$mz, x$intensity, type='l',
	main='combined spectra',
	xlab='m/Z', ylab='ion intensity')

xy <- peakdetection(x=x$mz, y=x$intensity, 
    scales=1:10, 
    SNR.Th=1.0, 
    SNR.area=20, mintr=0.5)

id.peakcenter<-xy[,4]

filter.mz <- 400 < x$mz & x$mz < 450
plot(x$mz[filter.mz], x$intensity[filter.mz], 
    main='Detection of relevant masses',
    type='l',
    xlab='m/Z', 
    ylab='ion intensity')

points(x$mz[id.peakcenter], 
    x$intensity[id.peakcenter], 
    col='red', type='h')

# create dummy object
xs@peaks <- matrix(c(rep(1, length(my.input.files) * 6), 
	1:length(my.input.files)), ncol=7)

colnames(xs@peaks) <- c("mz", "mzmin", "mzmax", "rt", 
	"rtmin", "rtmax", "sample")

xs <- xcms::retcor(xs, method="obiwarp", profStep=1, 
	distFunc="cor", center=1)

eicmat <- eicmatrix(xs=xs, xy=xy, center=1)

#
#  process a reduced mz range for a better package build performance
(eicmat.mz.range <- range(which(475 < xy[,1] & xy[,1] < 485)))

eicmat.filter <- eicmat[eicmat.mz.range[1]:eicmat.mz.range[2],]
xy.filter <- xy[eicmat.mz.range[1]:eicmat.mz.range[2],]

#
# determine the new range and plot the mz versus RT map
(rt.range <- range(as.double(colnames(eicmat.filter))))
(mz.range<-range(as.double(row.names(eicmat.filter))))

image(log(t(eicmat.filter))/log(2), 
    main='overlay of 12 samples using faahKO',
    col=rev(gray(1:20/20)),
    xlab='rt [in seconds]', 
    ylab='m/z', axes=FALSE)

axis(1, seq(0,1, length=6), 
    round(seq(rt.range[1], rt.range[2], length=6)))

axis(2, seq(0,1, length=4), 
    round(seq(mz.range[1], mz.range[2], length=4), 2))

#
# determine the chromatographic peaks
rxy <- retention_time(xs=xs, 
    RTscales=c(1:10, seq(12,32, by=2)), 
    xy=xy.filter, 
    eicmatrix=eicmat.filter, 
    RTSNR.Th=120, RTSNR.area=20)

rxy.rt <- (rxy[,4] - rt.range[1]) / diff(rt.range)
rxy.mz <- (rxy[,1] - mz.range[1]) / diff(mz.range)

points(rxy.rt, rxy.mz, pch="X", lwd=2, col="red")

xs <- create_datamatrix(xs=xs, rxy=rxy)

peaktable <- xcms::peakTable(xs)

idx <- order(rowSums(peaktable[,8:19]), decreasing=TRUE)
head(peaktable[idx,])
